judged_text: The Google Meet fallback dereferences the first element of destinationCalendar without checking it exists: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"`. Any booking with destinationCalendar null (the new default when neither eventType nor organizerUser has one, per handleNewBooking.ts line ~1064) or an empty array throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` during event creation, instead of falling back to Cal Video as before.

record.issue_text: [BUG] The Google Meet fallback dereferences the first element of destinationCalendar without checking it exists: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"`. Any booking with destinationCalendar null (the new default when neither eventType nor organizerUser has one, per handleNewBooking.ts line ~1064) or an empty array throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` during event creation, instead of falling back to Cal Video as before.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the new Google Meet fallback logic destructures `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then immediately dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without a null/undefined check. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` or `[]`, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and this will throw. The diff also shows `handleNewBooking.ts` can set `destinationCalendar` to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, and many other call sites now pass `[]`, making this crash reachable.
